expectation: Nuclear stain in cycling cells of any lineage. In gut-like tissue, expect many positive nuclei packed in the crypt and proliferative epithelial zone, plus scattered positive nuclei in lymphoid aggregates and stroma. Muscle should be negative.
observed: A: dense yellow dots form a band along the mucosal epithelium and the central lamina, with haze over the muscle. B: haze only. C: an epithelial ring with no positive nuclei, one blob in the lumen. D: one compact blob beside, not on, a nucleus.
why: At tissue scale the dots line the proliferative epithelial zone, but the cell-scale views never show clearly nuclear-filling positives, and most signal is haze or blobs.
notes: Ki67 dots cluster along the mucosal epithelial band, a plausible proliferative-zone pattern. Up close, B and C show only haze and the D cell is a compact blob not clearly in a nucleus, so the stain is low-contrast and uncertain.
